validated_results.title: Alcohol consumption, tobacco smoking, and subsequent risk of renal cell carcinoma: The JPHC study.
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort study evaluates the association between alcohol consumption and the risk of incident renal cell carcinoma.

extraction.population: Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study (JPHC Study)

sample_size.excerpt: We identified 340 cases (230 men and 110 women) among 106 003 eligible participants (50 262 men and 55 741 women), who were followed for an average of 19.1 years for a cumulative total of 2 020 364 person‐years.
sample_size.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Baseline survey, paragraph 2

cases.excerpt: We identified 340 cases (230 men and 110 women) among 106 003 eligible participants (50 262 men and 55 741 women), who were followed for an average of 19.1 years for a cumulative total of 2 020 364 person‐years.

design.excerpt: Here, we evaluated the effects of alcohol consumption and tobacco smoking on RCC incidence in a large Japanese prospective cohort.

timing.excerpt: We collected data on eligible participants in the Japan Public Health Center‐based Prospective Study, and undertook multivariable‐adjusted Cox proportional hazards regression to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of RCC incidence.

continent.excerpt: The protocol of the Japan Public Health Center‐based Prospective Study (JPHC Study) has been reported in detail elsewhere.
continent.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Study population, paragraph 1

ethnicity.excerpt: In brief, the JPHC Study began in 1990 (Cohort I) and 1993‐1994 (Cohort II) and included Japanese residents (n = 140 420) aged 40‐69 years from 11 public health center (PHC) areas.
ethnicity.location: MATERIALS AND METHODS, Study population, paragraph 1
